content: Orlistat is a medication prescribed to assist with weight loss when combined with a personalized low-calorie, low-fat diet and exercise program. It is used in overweight individuals, particularly those who may also have conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or heart disease. Additionally, it is prescribed to help prevent weight regain after initial weight loss. Orlistat belongs to a class of medications known as lipase inhibitors. It works in the intestines by blocking the absorption of some dietary fats, which are then excreted in the stool. Orlistat is available as a capsule and a non-prescription capsule, taken orally. It is typically taken three times a day with each main meal that contains fat. It should be taken during the meal or up to one hour after eating. If a meal is skipped or contains no fat, the dose can be skipped. Follow the instructions on your prescription or package label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take orlistat exactly as directed and do not take more or less than prescribed. If prescribed, ask your pharmacist or doctor for a copy of the manufacturer’s patient information. Orlistat may sometimes be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information if needed. Before taking orlistat, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to orlistat or any other medications. Discuss with your doctor if you are taking medications that suppress the immune system, such as cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune). If you are taking cyclosporine, it should be taken two hours before or two hours after orlistat. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and non-prescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), diabetes medications such as glipizide (Glucotrol), glyburide (DiaBeta, Micronase), metformin (Glucophage), insulin, medications for blood pressure control, thyroid disease, or other weight-loss medications. Inform your doctor if you have had an organ transplant, cholestasis (a condition where bile flow from the liver is blocked), or malabsorption syndrome (difficulty absorbing food). Your doctor may advise against taking orlistat in these cases. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have or have had an eating disorder (e.g., anorexia nervosa or bulimia), diabetes, kidney stones, pancreatitis (inflammation of the pancreas), or gallbladder or thyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, do not take orlistat. Follow the diet program provided by your doctor. Distribute your daily intake of fat, carbohydrates, and protein evenly across three main meals. Avoid high-fat meals or diets containing more than 30% of daily calories from fat, as this increases the likelihood of experiencing side effects. Orlistat blocks the absorption of some fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and beta-carotene. Therefore, take a daily multivitamin containing these vitamins. Read the label to ensure the multivitamin includes these nutrients, and take it once daily, either two hours before or after taking orlistat, or at bedtime. Consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have questions about taking a multivitamin while on orlistat. Avoid foods with more than 30% fat, and read food labels carefully. When consuming meat, poultry, or fish, limit servings to 2–3 ounces (about the size of a deck of cards). Choose lean cuts of meat, remove poultry skin, and prioritize grains, fruits, and vegetables. Replace whole-milk products with nonfat or low-fat alternatives, and cook with less fat, using vegetable oil spray when necessary. Opt for low-fat or nonfat versions of salad dressings, baked goods, and processed or fast foods, or reduce portion sizes. When dining out, inquire about food preparation methods and request minimal or no added fat. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it has been more than one hour since your last main meal. If it has been longer than one hour, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Orlistat may cause side effects, with the most common being changes in bowel habits, particularly during the initial weeks of treatment. These may include oily spotting on underwear or clothing, gas with oily discharge, an urgent need for bowel movements, loose stools, oily or fatty stools, increased bowel movements, difficulty controlling bowel movements, rectal pain or discomfort, stomach pain, irregular menstrual periods, headache, or anxiety. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or severe or continuous abdominal pain. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store orlistat in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat, moisture, and light (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and maintain a regular exercise program while taking orlistat. Consult your doctor before starting any new physical activity or exercise regimen. Do not share your prescription medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
